messages:
anna_k: quick summary — ran a cross-arch attention audit this morning. comparing FlashX (our new variant), FlashPaged, and the fused-CUDA kernel on SM80 vs SM90 across CUDA 11/12.

liam_r: nice. what was the workload? seq lengths / batch config?

anna_k: mostly mixed seq distribution from call-trace: 64% <= 512, 30% 512-2048, 6% >2048. tests: synthetic steady-state and a replay of prod traces. batcher = continuous batching with 10ms latency target, dynamic batch size up to 64.

marta_s: did you toggle KV paged vs full-KV? curious about memory pressure.

anna_k: yes. two modes: full-KV (single contiguous cache) and paged-KV with 256KB page size. paged reduces peak VRAM by ~12-18% on long sequences but adds ~1-3% token-latency due to page lookups for >2k sequences.

perf-bot: summary snapshot: FlashX(CUDA kernel, SM90, CUDA12): throughput 1.08x vs baseline FlashPaged(CUDA11, SM80). Fused-Triton(SM90,CUDA12) shows 0.92x on longseq (>4096).

liam_r: whoa fused-Triton < 1 on SM90 longseq. any idea why?

anna_k: profiling shows huge register spill and >40% stall cycles on SM90 for the Triton fused kernel at seq>2k. CUDA kernel (FlashX) reduces register usage by splitting dgrad loops and uses async copy -> lower stall.

anna_k: here's a short perf sample (throughput tokens/s) from the replay:```
workload       | FlashX(SM90,C12) | FlashPaged(SM80,C11) | Fused-Triton(SM90,C12)
-------------- | ----------------- | --------------------- | ---------------------
median(<=512)  | 1.12x             | 1.00x                 | 1.05x
512-2048       | 1.05x             | 1.00x                 | 0.98x
>4096          | 0.96x             | 1.00x                 | 0.92x
```

rachel_m: interesting that FlashX drops a bit on >4k. memory-bound?

anna_k: yes partly. FlashX uses a tiled KV gather that trades extra DRAM reads for compute reuse. At extreme seq it hurts because the working set exceeds L2 and we see more Lmem traffic. paged-KV shines there since it reduces resident KV pages.

dave_ops: what about CUDA version diffs — CUDA11 -> CUDA12. Any regressions?

anna_k: on SM80 we saw small-ish improvements moving to CUDA12 for our tiled CUDA kernel (2-4%), but on SM90 the Triton kernels regress unless we pin triton to nightly that has an SM90-specific scheduling fix. So spec: Triton mainline + CUDA12 = register alloc change causing spills.

liam_r: does the kernel selector currently prefer Triton on SM90?

anna_k: yes, selector uses heuristic: prefer Triton if arch>=sm90 and model size < 8B. That heuristic misses seq distribution and CUDA version effects. We need to weight by 1) median seq, 2) KV mode, 3) cuda-toolkit version, 4) observed stall% from recent traces.

marta_s: propose we augment the selector score: add terms (seq_tail_factor, kv_paged_bias, cuda_toolkit_penalty, register_spill_metric). small bump for FlashX on cuda12 when seq_tail>0.05.

rachel_m: can we add an auto-fallback: if observed latency p99 > target or stall% > 35% for 1min, switch to alternative kernel with warmup tolerance?

anna_k: implemented a prototype fallback: monitors per-kernel stall% and p99, then does attempt_cold_switch with 10s canary. works in replay but needs safety for stateful KV on live traffic. paged-KV mode requires sticky routing to same host to maintain page table state.

dave_ops: KV sticky routing constraint is important. any plan to do page-table sync across hosts?

anna_k: short term — prefer fallback only when both source and target support identical KV mode. long term — lightweight page-table sync RPC + bloom-filter to reduce traffic.

liam_r: re batching heuristics — did you try lowering continuous-batch latency target to favor smaller batches on longseq?

anna_k: yes. lowering latency SLO from 10ms -> 6ms shifted batcher to smaller batches, reducing tail latency at cost of 6-8% throughput. It improved fused-Triton p99 on SM90 (fewer big batches triggering register pressure), but FlashX throughput dropped slightly.

marta_s: action items?

anna_k: 1) update kernel selector to include cuda_toolkit and seq distribution signals (PR incoming).
2) add canary fallback flow guard for KV-compatible kernels (RFC this week).
3) test Triton nightly + CUDA12 scheduling fix on CI and run longseq stress for 48h.
4) perf-bot: schedule weekly replay for top-10 customer traces to collect stall% metrics.

perf-bot: noted: created ticket PERF-4512 for weekly replay and PERF-4513 for selector change.

liam_r: thanks. can you paste the profiling flame next? the one with L2 miss heatmap.

anna_k: will drop in #eng-runtime-artifacts in 15m — it's ~2MB. short snippet here: "L2 hit rate drops from 78% -> 54% when seq>4096 under FlashX tiled gather"

rachel_m: great context. once selector patch lands let's run a 2-day canary on dedicated pool. :thumbsup:

anna_k: agreed. ping me if you want access to the replay dataset.

liam_r: thanks everyone. closing thread after PRs land.
